data.description:
Rebuild the four lifecycle marks so every state is distinguishable by SHAPE alone, with no reliance on color or opacity.

Spec: docs/c11-mark-vocabulary.md
Live mock: scratchpad/mark-vocabulary-candidates.html

## Why

Working and waiting are both solid squares today, separated by hue alone. The in-code comment at vendor/bonsplit/.../TabItemView.swift:160 claims the set "survives greyscale and a color-blind reader"; that claim is false for exactly that pair. A real accessibility defect independent of any feature.

It also blocks the flagged/suppressed agents ticket, which needs the color channel free for a violet recolor.

## The set

- working = 3x3 dot grid over a faint base square
- waiting (needs attention) = 1.5pt heavy frame holding a 4pt solid core
- idle = 1pt thin empty frame
- cold = flat 2pt line

Marks pin to 9pt always. The sidebar's min(9, slot) compression to 8pt is removed; the mark row's slot floors at 9pt and the row yields width instead.

## Motion

Base motion ON by default, with a "Static marks" opt-out in Settings. Working dots tick in typewriter order (~4s cycle); needs-attention core dips (1.2s). Idle and cold never animate.

## Call sites

1. vendor/bonsplit/Sources/Bonsplit/Internal/Views/TabItemView.swift - TabActivityMark + TabActivityMarkMetrics. Keep this change PURE SHAPE VOCABULARY with no c11-specific concepts: it is a clean accessibility fix to offer upstream (almonk/bonsplit via manaflow-ai/cmux). Flag for upstream when the PR opens.
2. Sources/ContentView.swift - workspacePulseMark, plus the sidebar sizing rule at ~line 11324.

Colors (Sources/Workspace.swift) untouched.

## Performance contract (HARD SHIP BLOCKER)

Motion is default-on, so the typing-latency gate blocks merge.

1. MEASURE AT FLEET SCALE. Every working agent animates in TWO renderers at once (tab chip + sidebar mark row). A 20-agent fleet is 40+ animating leaf views. A single-mark test proves nothing.
2. ONE SHARED CLOCK, per-mark phase offset by a stable hash of surface id. Not N independent timers.
3. PAUSE OFF-SCREEN AND IN BACKGROUND. Unselected workspaces, collapsed panes, tabs scrolled out of the tab bar, app not active. SwiftUI does not do this for you.
4. VALIDATE THE LADDER ORDER EMPIRICALLY. Stated degradation is dip-only default, then static default. Probably correct because the dip is a pure opacity change the render server can composite without re-evaluating body, while the dot fill changes which shapes are drawn and forces body re-evaluation. Probably, not certainly. Measure both independently.

Each animated mark leaf-isolated with its own @State so repaints cannot invalidate the tab row or workspace card (TabItemView relies on Equatable + .equatable() to skip body re-evaluation during typing).

Reduce Motion (NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion) is a hard override: no mark animates when true, regardless of settings.

## Done when

- Both renderers draw the new set and agree
- All four states distinguishable in greyscale
- Marks hold at 9pt with no compression
- Static marks opt-out works
- Typing-latency gate passes at fleet scale on a tagged build, or the ladder is applied and the outcome recorded
- bonsplit change flagged for upstream

data.body: Execution clarification from operator: flagged non-waiting marks use normal lifecycle motion. Flagged working keeps the standard 4s block-fill animation; flagged idle and cold remain still. Skip a dedicated QA/performance harness and avoid an oversized test suite for now; preserve the shared-clock/leaf-isolation/offscreen-gating architecture and perform proportionate tagged-build validation.

Implementation started from clean ba1382a6c in isolated worktree codex/C11-183-mark-vocabulary. Expanded plan records the operator override: flagged working retains normal fill, flagged idle/cold stay still, only flagged waiting flashes; no dedicated performance harness.

Implementation handoff ready for review.

data.body: Trident plan review complete (9 reviewers + 4 syntheses). Verdict: revise-then-proceed. Plan rewritten to revision 2 with all apply-by-default findings absorbed — 4 blockers, 10 important, 13 mediums, 1 evolutionary clear win. Highlights: (B1) the plan's own c11-logic test command named a class that only exists in the host-bound c11Tests target — Phase 4 now pins target membership per file and lands new tests in c11LogicTests-member files; (B2) Bonsplit work restructured to one delivery: both logical commits pushed as a final HEAD to origin/main, ancestry proven, then a single parent pointer commit; (B3) <stage11-remote> placeholders replaced with origin; (B4) the operator's dropped 'perform proportionate tagged-build validation' clause restored, with a named validation-handoff section (owner, tagged launch path, fleet condition, fill/dip measured independently, ladder contingency, greyscale + light-theme + 1x acceptance). Also settled in rev 2: summary mark drops 10pt→9pt (deliberate visual change), exact phase tables for fill/dip/flash, suppressed-working = static full grid, single app-scope Reduce Motion observer, Static-marks propagation via BonsplitConfiguration.Appearance field, Equatable strategy per axis (modifiers via workspacePulse ==, environment axes leaf-local), FNV-1a phase offsets, MarkPresentation pure resolver + table test (EW1), WorkspacePulseAgent explicit init, Phase 0 worktree provisioning, doc-comment truthfulness in Bonsplit, translation follow-up ticket instead of a note. Skipping (evolutionary, out of scope for this pass): CLI text analogues for the four states in c11 tree/list (S9), general-purpose clock naming (E1), throughput-coupled fill (E2), DEBUG injectable phase source (E3) — all recorded in the pack for later. Full pack: notes/trident-review-C11-183-plan-pack-20260728-1327/ (9 reviews + synthesis-standard/adversarial/evolutionary/action). One complex decision flagged needs-human separately: clock ownership (S1).

data.reason: Clock ownership decision (S1) — settle before the delegator's Phase 2 Bonsplit commit; it is the plan's only expensive-to-reverse choice. 8 of 9 trident reviewers challenge putting the shared animation clock inside vendor/bonsplit and converge on the inverse: Bonsplit exports a pure public mark view taking phase as plain inputs (fillCount/coreOpacity, following the existing flashGeneration precedent), while c11 owns the clock, app-active gating, and Reduce Motion — where those APIs live. Claimed wins: geometry drift becomes structurally impossible (vs 'review the diff side by side'), the second submodule cycle disappears, and the upstream offer to almonk/bonsplit becomes an easier sell (shape, not a timer API). Cost: restructures Phases 1-2 and the revised plan should be re-reviewed. Plan rev 2 marks this OPEN DECISION at Phase 2 and requires the choice be recorded with reasoning either way. Secondary items worth a glance in synthesis-action.md 'Surface to user': S2 (how much validation protocol belongs in-plan), S3 (whether unreachable flag-tier visuals ship now or defer to C11-184; contact-sheet idea sits near your no-harness veto), S4 (does 'Static marks' really not silence flagged working?), S5 (do the six translations gate this ticket?), S6 (ship a three-value motion preference to pre-pay the ladder?).

data.body:
FAIL

Findings

1. HIGH — The Bonsplit delivery is not the required upstream-clean, pure shape vocabulary. vendor/bonsplit/Sources/Bonsplit/Internal/Views/TabItemView.swift:164-180 and 195-205 embed the c11-only flagged/suppressed model, hard-code c11's violet, and project suppressed waiting to idle. vendor/bonsplit/Sources/Bonsplit/Public/BonsplitActivityAnimationClock.swift:4-20 also owns c11's Static marks persistence key and flagged-waiting channel, while lines 99-123 reach directly into NSApp lifecycle. This makes the submodule API carry the downstream C11-184 product policy that the binding contract explicitly reserves for c11, so the claimed clean accessibility fix cannot be offered upstream independently. Smallest valid fix: keep Bonsplit shape rendering and any genuinely generic phase-input/clock primitive policy-free; move modifier resolution, violet, Static marks, app-active/Reduce-Motion ownership to c11 and inject plain effective state/tint/phase inputs into Bonsplit. If the timer engine remains in Bonsplit, it must be injected/host-driven and unaware of flagged, suppressed, c11 UserDefaults, and app-global policy; both renderers must still consume one instance.

2. MEDIUM — The offscreen gate counts marks hidden behind the opaque trailing controls as visible. vendor/bonsplit/Sources/Bonsplit/Internal/Views/TabBarView.swift:1274 passes the full containerWidth, and TabItemView.swift:766-772 tests intersection against that right edge. But TabBarView.swift:665-672 explicitly says trailing chrome visually obscures tabs underneath it. Any mark wholly inside that covered region remains registered and animates despite being invisible, violating the binding pause-offscreen performance rule. Smallest valid fix: supply/intersect against the actually visible tab-content rect (right edge before opaque chrome when shown, with minimal-mode hover state accounted for), then add a focused visibility-boundary test.

Evidence checked

- Complete parent diff ba1382a6c...d8b1ba2f3 and every changed parent file.
- Complete Bonsplit history/diff d4ff0e4c...d3d0fb586, including clock, leaf subscriptions, collapsed-tier call sites, viewport geometry, and tests.
- Static geometry and motion sampling against docs/c11-mark-vocabulary.md, the binding prototype, and the operator clarification: 9pt shapes agree; working reaches nine at about 3.6s and resets at 4s; waiting is 1.2s; flagged waiting is a core-only 0.4s hard flash; flagged working keeps fill; idle/cold stay still; suppression/flag/Static/Reduce-Motion precedence otherwise reads correctly.
- c11 TabItemView Equatable and .equatable() remain intact; no mark timer or TimelineView was added and hitTest/forceRefresh are untouched.
- Existing evidence logs: Bonsplit focused slice 4/4 passed; c11-logic projector slice 18/18 passed; c11-unit build-for-testing succeeded (compile/link only, correctly not treated as executed host tests); diff --check clean.
- Remote ancestry: local and remote Stage-11-Agentics/bonsplit main both resolve to d3d0fb586, and ancestry check succeeds.

Residual gates after the findings are fixed: tagged running-system inspection at true 9pt in both renderers, crowded-sidebar overflow, live Static marks and Reduce Motion transitions, and proportionate fleet-scale typing-latency comparison of fill versus dip. This review makes no visual, human-feel, or fleet-performance claim and does not transition task status.

Focused code review FAIL routed to implementation. Required contained fixes: (1) remove c11 flag/suppression/violet/Static-marks/app-lifecycle policy from Bonsplit so its exported mark/clock seam is generic and upstream-clean; c11 owns modifier composition and app policy. (2) correct viewport eligibility so marks obscured by opaque trailing chrome do not remain subscribed. Preserve the already-passing geometry, timing, one-clock, stable-phase, Reduce Motion, and projector behavior.

Blocker: minimal-mode hover visibility is still stale. TabBarView.swift:491-497 changes activityAnimationVisibleRightEdge when isHoveringTabBar changes, but TabItemView.swift:709-718 recalculates isActivityMarkVisible only on mark-frame appear/change; the frame need not change when hover chrome appears or disappears. Therefore a newly covered mark can remain registered/animated, and a newly uncovered mark can remain static. The helper-only test at BonsplitTests.swift:1544-1584 does not exercise that reactive transition. Recompute visibility when either frame OR visible-right-edge changes, with focused transition coverage.

data.body:
Resolved narrow reactive-visibility FAIL ev_01KYMYKJ59E4HJTE8W8TAGN8RR.

The existing mark GeometryReader now observes one Equatable production input containing both its current named-space frame and activityAnimationVisibleRightEdge. A scroll/frame change or a minimal-mode hover chrome edge change therefore runs the same leaf-local visibility callback. The callback still mutates only the mark leaf visibility state when the Boolean result changes; no timer, row observer, or row-wide animation invalidation was added.

Focused transition coverage holds the mark frame stationary while changing only the visible right edge, proving the input changes and visibility flips from true to false.
